# quest-teleop

> Generic VR teleoperation for Meta Quest headsets: a native OpenXR + OpenGL ES 3 headset app (C++, no game engine,
> no Gradle; standard OpenXR, tested on a Quest 2) and a pip-installable Python library (numpy only) that streams any 3D scene to the headset, receives
> both controllers every display frame, sends haptics and text cues, shows an in-headset panel with your own
> actions, records takes, and serves a local status page with a trajectory viewer. Includes a desktop test client
> and a demo.

- Repository: https://github.com/EntangledQuantum/quest-teleop (MIT licence), version 0.2.0
- Headsets: Meta Quest headsets through standard OpenXR (manifest: Quest 2, Quest Pro, Quest 3, Quest 3S); tested on a Quest 2
- Install the library: `pip install git+https://github.com/EntangledQuantum/quest-teleop` (Python 3.10+). Commands: `quest-teleop-demo`, `quest-teleop-probe`
- Build and install the headset app (Linux, from a clone): `android/setup_toolchain.sh` then `android/build_apk.sh install`
- Network: TCP 47800 and UDP 47800-47801 open on the computer, or `adb reverse tcp:47800 tcp:47800` over USB
- Status page: http://localhost:8800 while the demo or your server runs
- Every page below is plain Markdown; the same page as HTML is at the same path with `.html`

## Instructions for agents

Setting up quest-teleop for a user, in order:

1. Install the Python library and check it: `python -c "import quest_teleop; print(quest_teleop.__version__)"`.
   This alone is enough to run `quest-teleop-demo` and check it with `quest-teleop-probe` (no headset).
2. For the headset app, clone the repository and run `android/setup_toolchain.sh`. Tell the user first: it
   downloads about 2.4 GB into `~/android-sdk` and accepts the Android SDK licence agreements on their behalf.
   It needs cmake, make, curl, unzip, zip and Java 17+ (see Install).
3. Some steps need the user in person; ask them to do these and to tell you when done: enable developer mode in the
   Meta Horizon phone app; plug in the headset, put it on, tap "USB detected" and allow; accept "Allow USB
   debugging"; turn "Link auto connect" off. Then check `adb devices` lists the headset as `device`.
4. Some steps need root: the udev rule on Linux and the firewall ports. Show the user the exact command and ask
   before running anything with sudo. Over USB (`adb reverse`), the firewall change is not needed.
5. `android/build_apk.sh install`, then `quest-teleop-demo`, then start the app in the headset (Library, Unknown
   sources, labelled "Quest Teleop"). The status
   page at http://localhost:8800 (or `curl -s http://localhost:8800/api/state`) shows whether the headset connected.
6. To connect the user's own simulator or robot, follow "Use it with your own simulator" (a complete runnable
   example is at the top) and "Recording takes".
7. If something fails, read Troubleshooting before changing anything.

## Docs

- [Overview](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/index.md): What quest-teleop is, its parts, and the order to read these pages in.
- [Install](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/install.md): Install the Python library with pip; install the Android toolchain, build the APK and install it on the headset; build the desktop client; run the tests.
- [Headset setup](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/quest-setup.md): Written for and tested on a Quest 2: developer mode, the USB detected / allow USB debugging prompts, Link auto connect off, the udev rule on Linux, firewall ports TCP 47800 and UDP 47800-47801, USB link with adb reverse, launch options.
- [Quick start](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/quick-start.md): Run the bundled demo, connect the headset, the desktop client or the probe, the controls, record a take and open it on the status page.
- [Use it with your own simulator](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/library.md): The Python API: Scene, TeleopServer, controller input, haptics, text cues, the headset panel and actions, safe hand-to-tool mapping, the go-back cue, latency measurement.
- [Recording takes](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/recording.md): TakeRecorder, the files on disk, every array in a take, and loading takes.
- [Status page and trajectory viewer](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/status-page.md): The local web page: what it shows, the extra callback, the trajectory viewer, the JSON endpoints.
- [Protocol](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/protocol.md): The wire format, version 1: TCP and UDP channels, discovery, session, datagrams, state delta scheme, TCP messages, panel.
- [Measurements](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/measurements.md): Latency and bandwidth on loopback and on a Quest 2, over USB and Wi-Fi.
- [Troubleshooting](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/troubleshooting.md): The headset does not appear in adb, the build fails, the app does not find the server, nothing moves, high latency, the status page does not open.
- [FAQ](https://entangledquantum.github.io/quest-teleop/docs/faq.md): Supported headsets, engines, Link, operating systems, Wi-Fi or USB, bandwidth, several headsets, own clients, privacy, licence.
